 
Surgical  Technologist  Event  Category:  Health  Professions

Eligible  Divisions:  Secondary  &  Postsecondary/Collegiate   
Round  One:  50  Q  test  (60  minutes)  Digital  Upload:  NO  
Solo  Event:  1  competitor  Round  Two:  Skill(s)  assessment

surgical

Event  Summary
 The  Surgical  Technologist  event  allows  members  to  gain  essential  knowledge  and  skills  required  for  the  ﬁeld  of  Surgical  
Technology.
 
This
 
competitive
 
event
 
consists
 
of
 
two
 
rounds.
 
Competitors
 
will
 
take
 
a
 
written
 
test
 
for
 
Round
 
One.
 
Top-scoring
 
competitors
 
will
 
advance
 
to
 
Round
 
Two
 
for
 
a
 
clinical
 
skills
 
assessment.
 
This
 
event
 
aims
 
to
 
inspire
 
members
 
to
 
learn
 
more
 
about
 
Surgical
 
Technologist
 
careers,
 
enhance
 
critical
 
thinking
 
skills,
 
and
 
prepare
 
to
 
become
 
allied
 
health
 
professionals
 
capable
 
of
 
effectively
 
assisting
 
in
 
surgical
 
settings.
  
Sponsorship
 
HOSA-  Future  Health  Professionals  appreciates  the  sponsorship  of  this  event  by  the  Association  of  Surgical  Technologists.  
  
General  Event  Information
 
General  Rules   Competitors  must  be  familiar  with  and  adhere  to  the  General  Rules  and  Regulations.  
Dress  Code  Proper  business  attire  or  ofﬁcial  HOSA  uniform.  Bonus  points  will  be  awarded  for  proper  dress.   ●  Round  One:  Proper  business  attire,  ofﬁcial  HOSA  uniform,  or  attire  appropriate  to  the  occupational  area.    ●  Round  Two:  Attire  appropriate  to  the  occupational  area. 
Competitors  Must  Provide  ●  A  photo  ID for  both  rounds   ●  Two  #2  lead  pencils  (not  mechanical)  with  eraser  for  the  test.  ●  Neon  colored  foam  earplugs,  NOT  earbuds,  for  noise  control  (Rd1-optional)  ●  Sterile  Surgical  Gloves  (x2)   ●  surgical  cap  or  bouffant  cap   ●  Level  3  sterile  surgical  gown   ●  shoe  coverings   ●  Surgical  tie  mask,  Surgical  eye  protection,  safety  glasses,  eye  shield,  or  face  guard   ●  Surgical  scrub  brush  (no  soap)  HOSA  Conference  Staff  will  provide  equipment  and  supplies  listed  in  Appendix  I.  
Ofﬁcial  References   The  references  below are used  in  the  development  of  the  test  questions  and  skill  rating  sheets:   
 Surgical  Technologist  ILC  Guidelines  (September  2026)         Page  1  of  10  The  expectation  is  that  competitors  read  and  are  aware  of  all  the  content  within  these  guidelines  and  associated  links.  Successful  competitors  will  study  all  links  for  the  detailed  information.   

 a.  Association  of  Surgical  Technologists.  Surgical  Technolog y  for  the  Surgical  Technologists:  A  Positive  Care  Approach .   Cengage  Learning.   Latest  edition. (Rd1  Test  will  focus  on  Chapters  1,  4,  7,  10,  11,  and  16)  b.  Renee  Nemitz.  Surgical  Instrumentation:  An  Interactive  Approach.  Saunders.  Latest  edition.  
ROUND  ONE-  Test
 
Test  Instructions  All  competitors  will  be  given  a  test  and  answer  sheet.   The  written  test  will  consist  of  50  multiple-choice  items  in  a  maximum  of  60  minutes.  See  test  instructions  here. 
Time  Remaining  Announcements  
There  will  be  NO  verbal  announcements  for  time  remaining  during  ILC  testing.   All  ILC  testing  will  be  completed  in  the  Testing  Center,  and  competitors  are  responsible  for  monitoring  their  own  time.  
Written  Test  Plan  The  test  plan  for  the  Surgical  Technologist  is:  ●  Profession  of  CST-  10%  ●  Physical  Environment  and  Safety  Standards-  10%  ●  Surgical  Asepsis  and  Sterility-  20%  ●  Instrumentation,  Equipment,  and  Supplies-  30%  ●  Hemostasis,  Wound  Healing,  and  Wound  Closure-  10%  ●  Surgical  Anatomy  &  Physiology-  20%  
Sample  Test  Questions  1.  What  is  the  name  of  the  ﬁbrous  and  serous  capsule  that  covers  the  liver?  (AST,  pg  515,  CH  16)  A.  Bowman’s  B.  Glisson’s  C.  Tenon’s  D.  Articular  2.  Contamination  caused  by  the  passage  of  microorganisms  through  a  sterilized  package  by  way  of  moisture  wicking  is  termed:  (AST,  pg  134,  CH  7)  A.  Saturation  B.  Strike-through  C.  Solubilization  D.  Sequestration  3.  Weitlaner,  )’Conner-O’Sullivanh,  and  Balfour  are  examples  of:  (AST,  pg  267,  CH  10)  A.  Bone-holding  forceps  B.  Handheld  Retractors  C.  Non-Crushing  Clamps  D.  Self-Retaining  Retractors              
 Surgical  Technologist  ILC  Guidelines  (September  2026)         Page  2  of  10  The  expectation  is  that  competitors  read  and  are  aware  of  all  the  content  within  these  guidelines  and  associated  links.  Successful  competitors  will  study  all  links  for  the  detailed  information.   
 
ROUND  TWO-  Presentation  to  Judges
 
1.  The  top  competitors  from  Round  One  will  advance  to  Round  Two.  The  number  of  advancing  competitors  will  be  determined  by  the  scores  obtained  in  Round  One  and  the  space  and  time  available  for  Round  Two.  Round  Two  ﬁnalists  will  be  announced  on-site  at  ILC  per  the  conference  agenda.  
2.  Round  Two  is  a  selected  skill(s)  assessment.  The  skills  approved  for  this  event  are:  
Skill  I:  Identify  Instruments/Equipment  (see  list  below)  15  minutes  
Skill  II:  Surgical  Scrub  Methods  6  minutes  
Skill  III:  Open  Gloving  Techniques  3  minutes  
Skill  IV:  Gowning  &  Gloving  (Self)   5  minutes  
Skill  V:  Passing  Surgical  Instruments 5  minutes  
Skill  VI:  Loading  &  Passing  Surgical  Sutures 4  minutes  3.  For  all  skills,  body  ﬂuids  will  be  a  simulated  product.   
Below  is  the  list  of  equipment  used  for  the  Skill  I:  Identify  Instruments/Equipment.  This  skill  may  be  included  with  the  Round  One  written  test,  to  include  15  numbered  photos  of  instruments  and  or  equipment..   If  this  skill  is  administered  with  
the
 
Round
 
One
 
written
 
test,
 
the
 
skill
 
assessment
 
allotted
 
time
 
will
 
be
 
added
 
to
 
the
 
written
 
test
 
allotted
 
time.
  
 Electrosurgical  Pencil  Harrington  Sweetheart  Retractor  
 Adson  Tissue  Forceps  Kocher-Ochsner  Clamp

4.  The  selected  skill(s)  will  be  presented  to  competitors  as  a  written  scenario  at  the  beginning  of  the                round.  The  scenario  will  be  the  same  for  each  competitor.  Some  scenarios  may  involve  the  combination                of  multiple  skills.  In  the  event  rating  sheets  are  combined,  it  is  not  necessary  to  repeat  a  task  a  second                time.  An  example  would  be  that  competitors  would  not  need  to  identify  the  patient  twice.  A  sample                scenario  is  available  here.  
5.  Timing  will  begin  when  the  scenario  is  presented  to  the  competitors  and  will  be  stopped  at  the  end  of  the  time  allowed.  The  scenario  is  a  secret  topic.  Competitors  MAY  NOT  discuss  or  reveal  the  secret  topic  until  after  the  event  has  concluded  or  will  face  penalties  per  the  GRRs.   
6.  Competitors  must  complete  all  skill  steps  listed  in  the  guidelines,  even  if  the  steps  must  be                simulated/verbalized.  (If  the  equipment  is  available,  the  competitors  would  complete  all  skill  steps  as  the               scenario  warrants.  The  competitors  will  simulate/verbalize  the  steps  if  the  equipment  is  unavailable.)  
7.  Judges  will  provide  information  to  competitors  as  directed  by  the  rating  sheets.  Competitors  may                ask  questions  of  the  judges  while  performing  skills,  if  the  questions  relate  to  patient’s  condition  and                will  be  included  in  the  scenario  or  judge  script.  
 Surgical  Technologist  ILC  Guidelines  (September  2026)         Page  3  of  10  The  expectation  is  that  competitors  read  and  are  aware  of  all  the  content  within  these  guidelines  and  associated  links.  Successful  competitors  will  study  all  links  for  the  detailed  information.   
 8.  Competitors  must  use  all  equipment  correctly  and  safely.  Judges  will  stop  a  student  and  not  award  points  for  a  step  if  they  see  a  competitor  is  about  to  cause  a  risk  of  harm  or  about  to  damage  equipment  or  other  supplies.   
Final  Scoring 
 1.  The  competitor  must  earn  a  score  of  70%  or  higher  on  the  combined  skill(s)  in  Round  Two-Skill  Assessment   
(excluding
 
              the  test  and  ID  equipment)  in  order  to  be  recognized  as  an  award  winner  at  the  ILC.    2.  The  ﬁnal  rank  is  determined  by  adding  the  round  one  test  score  plus  the  round  two  skill  score.  In  the  event  of  a  tie,  
the
 
highest
 
test
 
score
 
will
 
be
 
used
 
to
 
determine
 
the
 
ﬁnal
 
placement.
  
Final  Opportunities
 The  HOSA  Scholarship  program  has  funding  available  for  HOSA  members  who  have  an  interest  in  various  health  careers!  The  application  process  begins  January  1,  2027,  and  can  be  found  here: https://hosa.org/scholarships/.   Graduating  from  high  school  or  completing  your  postsecondary/collegiate  program  does  not  mean  your  HOSA  journey  has  to  
end.

Surgical  Technologist  Skill  II:  Surgical  Scrub  Methods
 
Time:  6  minutes  
Competitor   #: __________________________  Division:  ______ SS ______ PS/Collegiate     Judge’s  Signature: __________________________
 
 Skill  II:  Surgical  Scrub  Methods  Possible  Awarded      1.    Assembled  equipment.  
1  0  
  
    2.    Donned  all  PPE   a.  Tucked  in  scrub  top  
1  0  
  
b.  Rolled  sleeves  up  2”  above  elbows  
2  0  
  3.   Removed  any  jewelry  
2  0  
  
4.   Inspected  the  integrity  of  hands  and  arms  to  rule  out  presence  of  non-intact  skin  
2  0  
  
5.   Inspected  nails  and  cuticles  
2  0  
  6.   Open  brush  package  and  place  in  convenient  location  
2  0  
  
7.   Turned  on  water  to  wet  hands  and  arms  and  lather  2”  above  elbows   
2  0  
  8.   Used  the  nail  cleaner  to  carefully  clean  subungual  areas  of  both  hands  while  holding  the    hand  under  the  running  water  
2  0  
  
9.   Discarded  the  nail  cleaner  in  the  proper  receptacle.   
2  0  
  10.   Unwrapped  the  scrub  sponge  and  dispense  soap  unless  sponge  is impregnated  with  soap  
2  0  
  11.   Started  timing  or  counting  strokes  scrub  technique  (2  minutes  per  arm)  
2  0  
  
12.   Began  scrub  with  the  nails,  passed  ﬁngernails  back  and  forth  across  the sponge.   
2  0  
  
 a.  Kept  hands  above  elbows  and  elbows  bent  to  allow  water  to  run  off  
2  0  
  
b.  Each  ﬁnger  has  four  planes.  Scrubbed  each  plane  of  each  ﬁnger  individually,  between  the  ﬁngers  in  the  web  spaces.   
2  0  
  
c.  Divided  arm  into  three  sections  with  four  planes  up  to  2”  above  elbow.  
2  0  
  13.   Transferred  brush  to  the  scrubbed  hand  and  repeated  the  process  on  the  opposite  extremity   before  discarding  the  brush  
2  0  
  
14.   Rinsed  one  extremity  from  the  ﬁngertips  to  elbow  while  keeping  elbows bent  and  hands    above  elbow.  
2  0  
  
 a.  Avoided  touching  body,  faucet,  and  sides/edges  of  sink.   
2  0  
  
b.  Repeated  rinse  on  opposite  extremity.   
2  0  
  15.   Proceeded  to  the  operating  room  (O.R.)  with  elbows  bent  and  hands  between  mid-chest  and   waist  level.  
2  0  
  
 a.  Entered  O.R.  by  opening  door  by  turning  back  to  the  door,  pushing  it open,  and  rotating  into  the  operating  room  
2  0  
  
 b.  Did  not  touch  anything  including  scrub  suit,  one  arm  to  other,  crossed  arms,  until  gowned  and  gloved  
2  0  
  
 c.  Kept  elbows  ﬂexed  and  proceeded  to  gown  and  glove  
2  0  
  
 
             
* Judge  states  “ Skill  completed ”.   
Total  Points-  Skill  II:   
70%
 
Mastery
 
for
 
Skill
 
II:
 
32.2
 
46

Surgical  Technologist   Skill  III:  Open  Gloving  Technique  Time:  3  minutes  
Competitor   #: ___________________________  Division:  ______ SS ______ PS/Collegiate   Judge’s  Signature: __________________________
 
 Skill  III:  Open  Gloving  Technique  
Possible  Awarded  
1.   Assembled  equipment.  
1  0  
  
2.   Removed  any  jewelry   
2  0  
  
3.   Wa shed  hands  or  used  alcohol-based  hand-rub  for  hand  hygiene.  
2  0  
  
4.   Opened  outer  non-sterile  wrapper  and  delivered  the  inner  sterile  wrapped gloves  onto  a    clean,  dry  surface  
2  0  
  
5.   Opened  the  inner  wrapper  to  create  a  small  sterile  ﬁeld,  up  to  2”  of  the perimeter  are   considered  nonsterile   
2  0  
  
 a.  Touched  only  the  outer  edges  of  the  inside  wrapper   
2  0  
  
b.  Secured  the  ﬁrst  glove  from  the  wrapper  by  pinching  the  cuffed  edge  and  lifted  the  glove  up  and  away  from  the  wrapper.   
2  0  
  
c.  Oriented  the  ﬁngertips  of  the  glove  downward.   
2  0  
  
6.   Applied  the  glove  to  the  opposite  hand  by  inserting  the  ﬁngers  and  pulling the  glove  over   the  palm  without  touching  the  glove  exterior.  
2  0  
  
7.   Unfolded  the  cuff  of  the  glove  without  touching  the  exterior.  
2  0  
  
8.   Retrieved  the  second  glove  from  the  wrapper  by  inserting  the  ﬁngertips  of the  already  gloved   (sterile)  hand  under  the  cuffed  edge  of  the  glove.   
2  0  
  
9.   Kept  the  gloved  thumb  tucked  under  the  cuff  or  well  out  of  the  way.          
2  0  
  
10.   Lifted  the  glove  up  and  away  from  the  wrapper.  
2  0  
  
11.   Applied  the  glove  in  the  manner  previously  described,  making  minor  adjustments  without   touching  the  nonsterile  hand.  
2  0  
  
Total  Points-  Skill  III:  
70%
 
Mastery
 
for
 
Skill
 
III:
 
18.9
  
27

Surgical  Tecnologist  Skill  IV:  Gowning  and  Gloving  (Self)  Time:  5  minutes  
Competitor   #: ___________________________  Division:  ______ SS ______ PS/Collegiate   Judge’s  Signature: __________________________
 
 Skill  IV:  Gowning  and  Gloving  (Self)  
Possible  Awarded  
    1.    Approached  the  sterile  ﬁeld  with  caution.  
     2  0  
  
2.     Donning  Gown:  a.  Grasped  the  gown  at  the  center  neck  without  touching  the   glove  or  the wrap  
     2  0  
  
b.  Lifted  the  gown  from  the  wrapper  and  stepped  back  with  the  gown  still folded.  
     2  0  
  
c.  Held  the  inside  of  the  gown  near  the  shoulders  and  allowed  the  gown  to  unfold  (did  not  shake  gown  open)  
     2  0  
  
d.  Began  donning  the  gown  by  slipping  the  hands  and  arms  into  the  sleeves.  Slide  the  gown  over  the  arms  using  a  “swimming”  motion.  
     2  0  
  
3.   Keep  hands  within  the  cuff  of  the  gown.  Flex  the  elbows  to  hold  the  gown in  place.   
     2  0  
  
4.   Donning  Gloves:  a.  Begin  closed  gloving,  did  not  protrude  ﬁngers  outside  the   knitted  cuff  of  the  gown.  
     2  0  
  
 b.  Approached  the  sterile  ﬁeld  with  caution.   
     2  0  
  
c.  Opened  the  glove  wrapper,  grasped  the  two  center  edges,  opening outward  and  everting  package  slightly  to  expose  the  gloves  keeping  ﬁngers  from  entering  the  cuff  of  the  gown  
     2  0  
  
d.  Secured  the  ﬁrst  glove  without  ﬁngers  entering  the  cuff  of  the  gown.  
     2  0  
  
e.  Aligned  the  glove  on  the  palm  of  the  hand  that  will  be  gloved  ﬁrst  with thumb  side  of  the  glove  toward  your  palm  and  the  ﬁngertips  toward  your elbow.  
     2  0  
  
f.  Pulled  the  cuff  of  the  glove  over  the  cuff  of  the  gown.  
     2  0  
  
g.  Unfolded  the  cuff  of  the  glove  to  completely  cover  the  cuff  of  the  gown.  
     2  0  
  
h.  Grasped  the  glove  and  the  gown  at  the  wrist  level.  Worked  the  ﬁngers into  the  glove  as  the  glove  is  being  pulled  into  position.   
     2  0  
  
5.   Secured  the  second  glove  and  apply  using  closed  gloving  technique  with  the  other  hand.   
     2  0  
  
6.   Checked  both  gloved  hands  for  any  sign  of  punctures  or  tears.   
     2  0  
  
7.  
 
Repeated
 
process
 
to
 
always
 
ensure
 
double
 
gloved.
 
     2  0    
8.   Pulled  tie  to  release  from  paper  tab,  passed  the  gown  tab  to  the  Circulator  (judge)  and    turned,  securing  gown  ties.  
     2  0    
Total  Points-  Skill  IV:  
70%
 
Mastery
 
for
 
Skill
 
IV:
 
25.2
 
36

Surgical  Technologist  Skill  V:  Passing  Surgical  Instruments  Time:  5  minutes  
Competitor   #: ___________________________  Division:  ______ SS ______ PS/Collegiate    Judge’s  Signature: __________________________
 
 Skill  V:  Passing  Surgical  Instruments  
Possible  Awarded  
1.   Demonstrate  hand  signal:  hemostat,  forceps,  scissors,  suture,  scalpel  
2  0  
 
 2.    Properly  passed  Ringed  Instruments:  a.  Ensured  instruments  are  in  locked  position   
2  0  
 
  b.  Passed  by  holding  box  lock  of  instrument  and  placed  the  rings  in  the palm  of  the  surgeon’s  open  receiving  hand  using  a  quick  snap  of  the  wrist.  
2  0  
 
    3.   Passed  instruments  appropriately  in  accordance  to  where  the  Surgeon  is positioned:  a.  If  the  Surgeon  is  on  the  same  side  of  the  table  and  to  the  left  of  the  CST-  passed  to  Surgeon’s  right  hand  using  your  right  hand  and  passed  to Surgeon’s  left  hand  using  your  right  hand.   OR    b.  If  the  Surgeon  is  on  the  same  side  of  the  table  and  to  the  right  of  the CST-  passed  to  Surgeon’s  left  hand  using  your  left  hand,  and  passed  to Surgeon’s  right  hand  using  your  left  hand.    OR  c.  If  the  Surgeon  is  across  from  the  CST  -  passed  to  the  Surgeon's  right  or left  hand  depending  on  the  dominant  hand  of  the  Surgeon.               
2            
0  
 
 
              
 
*Judge  states which  hand  is  the  Surgeon’s  dominant. 
  
 4.   Properly  passed  Retractors:  a.  Placed  the  handle  of  the  hand-held  retractor  in  the  Surgeon's  hand.  
   2  0  
 
 
b.  Ensured  when  passing  the  retractor,  blade  was  pointed  toward  the patient’s  incision.   
    2  0  
 
 
    5.   Properly  passed  Sponge  Stick:  a.  Passed  sponge  stick  with  sponge  to  surgeon  demonstrating  immediate use.  
    2    0  
 
 
     6.    
 Properly  passed  Scalpel:  a.  Demonstrate  no-hands  technique where  scalpel  is  placed  in  a  neutral zone,  retrieved,  used  by  Surgeon,  and  returned  to  neutral  zone  
    2     0  
 
 
b.  Held  the  scalpel  on  top  above  blade  with  blade  facing  self  
   2  0  
 
 
c.  Used  thumb  and  index  ﬁnger  to  protect  blade     
   2  0  
 
 
d.  With  palm  of  the  passing  hand  facing  the  O.R.  table  and  the  scalpel  blade  edge  also  facing  toward  the  O.R.  table,  away  from  the  palm,  ensured  blade  rests  in  the  open  area  formed  by  the  cupped  hand.  
   2  0  
 
 
e.  Securely  placed  the  knife  hand  in  the  Surgeon’s  hand.  
   2  0  
 
 
f.  When  Surgeon  has  securely  grasped  the   blade,  moved  passing  hand  up  and  away  from  the  blade.  
    2  0  
 
 
Total  Points-  Skill  V:  
70%

Surgical  Technologist  Skill  VI:  Loading  and  Passing  Surgical  Sutures   Time:  4  minutes  
Competitor   #: ___________________________  Division:  ______ SS ______ PS/Collegiate    Judge’s  Signature: __________________________
 
 Skill  VI:  Loading  and  Passing  Surgical  Sutures   
Possible  Awarded  
    1.    Loaded  needle  at  the  tip  of  the  needle  holder  
2  0  
  
2.     Set  at  a  90-degree  angle  to  the  long  line  of  the  needle  holder,  ensuring  the correct  direction   for  left  or  right  handed  suturing  technique.   
2  0  
  
3.    Made  sure  the  box  is  fully  locked  before  passing.  
2  0  
  
4.    Treated  needle  holder  as  a  ring  instrument,  ensuring  it  is  passed  by grasping  the  lock  box   and  using  a  quick  snap  of  the  wrist  to  place  rings  in Surgeon’s  palm.              
2  0  
  
5.    Prior  to  passing,  suture  is  draped  over  the  back  of  your  hand  to  ensure  the delivering  hand   prohibits  the  suture  from  entering  the  Surgeon’s  hand  with the  instrument.  
2  0  
  
6.    Controlled  long  sutures  until  the  Surgeon  has  full  control  of  the  suture  to  prevent  suture   contamination.   
2  0  
  
7.    Ensured  a  neutral  zone  is  maintained  to  minimize  incidents  of  sharp   injury.  
2  0  
  
Total  Points-  Skill  VI:  
70%
